news.title: Binance Reports $6.34 Billion in Loss Coverage as Withdrawals Reopen in Phases
news.body: Binance said it committed more than $6.34 billion to replace assets affected by the late-October theft. PYMNTS reported that authorities and private-sector firms had frozen more than $2.7 billion in stolen assets while the exchange reopened withdrawals in phases. Committed replacement funding, frozen assets and money returned to customers measure different things; the coverage announcement alone does not establish how much stolen money Binance has recovered.

news.title: Fed Sets 2027 Payment-Service Prices With a 1.4% Average Increase
news.body: Banks and credit unions will receive new wholesale payment-service prices on January 1, 2027. The Federal Reserve estimates an average increase of 1.4% across its established, mature services. That aggregate is not a uniform increase for every service: each institution’s processing mix determines its cost change. The schedules establish wholesale costs, not equivalent increases in the fees banks charge customers.

news.title: OpenAI Introduces Tokenized ChatGPT Wallet Requiring User Approval for Every Purchase
news.body: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet with American Express, Mastercard and Visa for eligible adult U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers using eligible U.S.-issued cards. Users review every purchase and complete a security check; payment networks supply tokens rather than exposing card details to the agent. The wallet uses existing card acceptance and preserves card rewards and protections, making this AI-assisted checkout rather than unrestricted delegated spending.

news.title: Three Central Banks Test Coordinated FX Settlement Across Different Systems
news.body: Project Meridian FX APAC demonstrated coordination between real-time gross settlement (RTGS) systems, which settle payments individually, and distributed-ledger test environments. The Bank of England, Monetary Authority of Singapore and Bank of Thailand tested payment-versus-payment—exchanging both currencies only when both sides can settle—and multilateral net settlement, which offsets obligations among participants. Partior developed and tested the synchronization prototype. The trial did not launch a production service or establish production cost or speed savings; further development requires legal arrangements, oversight and an operating model.

source.name: Bank of England, joint central-bank release

news.title: PayPal Links Pending Bank Charter to Deposit Funding for Merchant Lending
news.body: PayPal CFO and operating chief Jamie Miller said a bank subsidiary would support merchant lending and diversify funding through consumer or commercial deposits. PayPal filed its application with the FDIC and Utah regulators in December 2025; it remains pending. Miller’s comments explain the proposed bank’s funding model, not a regulatory approval. Any financing advantage would depend on deposit costs, capital requirements and approval conditions, and PayPal has not announced that it will discontinue existing lending partnerships or loan-sale arrangements.

perspective: OpenAI adds user-approved card checkout, while PayPal outlines deposit-funded merchant lending under its pending bank application.

curiosity.text: Japan’s Zengin interbank network began operating in April 1973, linking banks to exchange domestic credit-transfer instructions; that milestone was not the origin of furikomi bank transfers.
